digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, App. VI (+ Mgombato doka)
other_mijikenda: Duruma, Giriama: same name 'Mbugubugu' (Pakia App. VI)

teaser.en: A forest Cissus, named by science only in 1993, whose young leaves come up crimson-purple.

summary.en: This mdokadoka is a forest liana of the grape family, found only on the coast of south-east Kenya and eastern Tanzania. Like its relatives it has fleshy leaves and brittle stems.

about.en: *Cissus sylvicola* is a liana that can climb to about 12 metres. It has tendrils and lateral roots that are often swollen into tubers. Its leaves are slightly to markedly fleshy and hairless, varying from diamond-shaped to oval or round, sometimes shallowly lobed. Young leaves are usually crimson-purple and turn green as they mature. Like other *mdokadoka*, its stem breaks easily, and Digo people identify it by the stem rather than the leaves.

where.en: It grows in evergreen forest, forest on rocky hills and coral limestone thicket, from near sea level to about 500 metres. Its range runs from south-east Kenya to eastern Tanzania. *Sylvicola* means 'forest-dweller'.

culture.en: Pakia explains *mdokadoka* as 'breaking', because the stem breaks (*doka*) easily, and *mbugubugu* as the basic Digo name for a climber.

names.en: Digo: *mdokadoka*, 'breaking', and *mbugubugu*, 'climber', shared with Duruma and Giriama. Pakia gives the same two names to *Cissus rotundifolia* and *C. quinquangularis*, so the Digo do not separate these three species by name. No English or Swahili name is recorded. Botanists described the species in the *Flora of Tropical East Africa* in 1993.

conservation.en: It has a small range, limited to coastal forest and thicket in Kenya and Tanzania. These are habitats under pressure from clearing, although the species has not been formally assessed as threatened.

reason.en: Rhoicissus, a forest relative in the grape family

mgombato: doka to tear, to break off, to come apart (e.g. a piece of rope); kukatika.
